claim: The jet of the reference leak (5 L/min at 3 bar) carries about 25 W of mechanical power, of which only a small fraction (1e-6 to 1e-4, assumed) becomes sound
law: Jet power = volume flow x pressure drop (Bernoulli)
check: claimed 25 W, estimate 25 W (ratio 1.00)

claim: A leak noise logger on a valve hears the reference leak 100 m along a ductile iron main
law: Fluid-dominated axial wave in a shell (Pinnington and Briscoe; Gao et al. 2004), flat leak spectrum, acoustic efficiency 1e-5 (assumed), 0.5 ug/rtHz background, valve coupling -10 dB (assumed). Signal equal to noise (LKL-CAL-001 G2) gives 185 m; the flag rule needs the level up 6 dB (leak 4.8 dB above the noise), which gives the value below; at efficiency 1e-6 / 1e-5 / 1e-4 it is 80 / 141 / 249 m. The mount's resonance (S6) is not applied to the signal

claim: The same contact sensor hears the reference leak 30 m along a PVC main
law: Axial attenuation on PVC DN150 is 0.42 dB/m at 100 Hz against 0.011 dB/m on ductile iron (LKL-CAL-001 E1); the central estimate is 4 m
check: 4 m against 30 m: the detail fails. Fix already decided by Amish (2026-09-25, LKL-DDR-002 D8): the contact sensor serves metallic mains only; plastic mains are served by a hydrophone (option B, S-B rows)

claim: The piezo charge amplifier reaches about 1 ug/rtHz equivalent input noise from 100 Hz to 1 kHz
law: Charge amplifier noise: voltage noise x total input capacitance, feedback resistor and ceramic loss noise, divided by charge sensitivity (53 g mass, d33 300 pC/N, 5 nV/rtHz op-amp, all assumed): 1.03 ug/rtHz worst against 1.0, so the order is right and the margin is nil. Noise scales as 1/d33. The 24-bit audio ADC is assumed to reach about 2 uV rms over 20 kHz (adds under 0.01 ug/rtHz); a 12-bit converter would add 0.1 ug/rtHz or more
check: Ceramic, op-amp and ADC datasheets of the chosen parts

claim: The piezo and seismic mass resonate far above the 2 kHz band
law: Spring-mass resonance, f = sqrt(k/m) / 2 pi, k of a 20 mm ceramic in compression (E 63 GPa)
check: 202 kHz >= 10 kHz

claim: The magnet-mounted sensor is flat within 3 dB from 5 Hz to 2 kHz after correction
law: The 277 g puck and magnet on the contact stiffness of a coated cap (5e6 to 2e7 N/m) resonate at 676 to 1,352 Hz, inside the band, and are flat only to 366 to 732 Hz (LKL-CAL-001 F6). A mounted resonance is a narrow peak that a digital equaliser can correct, if its frequency is known per mounting
check: Needs a shaker comparison of the mounted sensor (CalRig bay, decided 2026-10-02) at TRL 4; the contact stiffness is assumed

claim: One C-size lithium thionyl chloride cell runs the logger for 10 years
law: Charge budget: 7.7 Ah nominal x 0.70 usable (cold, pulses) divided by 3,650 days; daily charge from sleep, listening, radio, self-discharge and status light
check: 1.25 mAh/day <= 1.48 mAh/day

claim: A 0.1 F hybrid layer capacitor carries the radio pulse the cell cannot supply
law: C = (I_tx - I_cell_max) x airtime / allowed droop 0.5 V (3.6 V to 3.1 V); I_cell_max 30 mA for a C-size Li-SOCl2 cell with a hybrid capacitor (manufacturer data, to confirm)

claim: The lithium thionyl chloride cell keeps its capacity for 10 years at 2 to 20 degC and delivers the pulses after long rest (passivation)
law: Li-SOCl2 cells self-discharge about 1 % a year but build a passivation layer that lowers the first pulse voltage; a hybrid layer capacitor is the standard remedy (Saft and Tadiran application notes, to cite from the datasheets of the chosen cell)
check: Manufacturer datasheet and a pulse test of the chosen cell at TRL 4

claim: A LoRa uplink leaves a chamber under a cast-iron cover and reaches a gateway 0.5 km away
law: Link budget with Hata urban path loss, 10 dB fade margin and an assumed 20 dB cover loss: +0.9 dB at 0.5 km for EU868 SF12 (LKL-CAL-001 D5), -11.8 dB at 1 km for US915 SF9 is negative; the cover loss is unmeasured and a tight flooded cover (30 dB) fails; the Hata model is stated for 1 to 20 km, so 0.5 km is an extrapolation (independent review)
check: Cover loss to measure on a real chamber at TRL 4; gateway placement decided (LKL-DDR-002 D7)

claim: The 42 mm pot magnet holds the puck on a spindle cap with a 0.5 mm paint and rust gap
law: Pull force falls with the air gap as F = F_iron / (1 + g/g0)^2, g0 0.6 mm (a rule of thumb fitted to catalogue curves, assumed); 70 % of the rated pull on a typical cap; against 100 N (about 30 x the 3 N weight of the puck and 0.5 m of cable, LKL-CAL-001 I2); a straight pull-off only: shear or peel from a snagged cable or a knock, a sliding resistance near 0.2 x the pull, and the real contact area of a spindle cap smaller than the 42 mm pole face are not checked

claim: A flooded logger floats on its lanyard
law: Archimedes: logger mass against the mass of water displaced by its 63 x 240 mm body

claim: The 24-byte summary fits every LoRaWAN rate used (EU868 SF12 limit 51 B, US915 SF9 limit 53 B)
law: Application payload limits of the LoRaWAN Regional Parameters (TS001) with 13 B of protocol overhead already counted

claim: Random night-to-night variation (2 dB) raises fewer than 1 false flag per 20 loggers per month
law: Gaussian tail: flag at +6 dB for 3 independent nights, p = Q(6/sigma)^3, nights taken as independent (nightly minima are in fact correlated, and the 14-night baseline error is shared); real site noise (pumps, pressure reducing valves) is not random and is not covered
check: 1.5e-06 per 20 loggers per month <= 1 per 20 loggers per month

claim: Site noise (pumps, pressure reducing valves, night use) does not mimic a leak in a way a 14-night baseline cannot remove
law: Commercial noise loggers rely on night-time minimum levels and trends, and still produce false positives that need a follow-up survey (Gutermann, Hunaidi and Chu 1999)
check: Field data from a partner network at TRL 4

claim: Nothing in option A touches drinking water or changes its quality
law: The magnet sits on a spindle cap in the chamber air; the housing is PVC pipe outside the water; no part is fixed to the pipe. A design review, not a calculation
check: Confirmed by the model: no part of option A passes through a pipe wall

claim: A hydrophone on a hydrant cap hears the reference leak 30 m along a PVC main
law: Leak pressure in the water column (flat source spectrum, efficiency 1e-5, wave speed and attenuation of LKL-CAL-001 E1) against a 0.1 Pa/rtHz night background at 100 Hz and above, rising as 1/f below (assumed) and the tube's charge-amplifier noise (0.28 mPa/rtHz at 100 Hz); background 0.01 / 0.1 / 1 Pa/rtHz gives 497 / 54 / 0 m on PVC; PE100 at 0.1 Pa/rtHz 30 m; efficiency 1e-6 / 1e-5 / 1e-4 at 0.1 Pa/rtHz gives 17 / 54 / 172 m; the 6 dB flag rule is applied; branch and hydrant insertion losses are not

claim: The 16 mm stainless cap and four M12 bolts hold a 10 bar hydrant, with a 3 x margin
law: Simply supported circular plate, sigma = 3 (3 + nu) p r^2 / (8 t^2), nu 0.3, r 32 mm; the water acts on the 64 mm bore (the plate between the bore and the 170 mm bolt circle rests on the flange); bolt preload and gasket load are not included; bolts at 3.2 kN shared by four M12 (84.3 mm2); plate 4.9 MPa and bolts 10 MPa against the 205 MPa proof of 316 and 450 MPa of A4-70, both divided by 3
check: 0.07 ratio to proof <= 1 ratio to proof

claim: A stainless cap, EPDM gasket and PU-potted hydrophone do not change drinking water quality
law: Products in contact with drinking water need approval in many jurisdictions (UK Regulation 31, DWI and WRAS); stainless steel and EPDM grades with approvals exist, the potting compound and cable jacket do not yet have a chosen approved grade
check: Approved grades to select with the partner utility; not assessed here

claim: The cap bolts to the hydrant outlet
law: The model assumes a four-bolt 170 mm flange outlet (an assumption). Commercial hydrophone caps are made for threaded 2.5 inch outlets (SubSurface Enigma 3 kit lists 2.5 inch stainless hydrant caps); outlet type varies by country and utility
check: Outlet type and thread to confirm with the partner; the cap interface would be redesigned for it

claim: A geophone at 0.5 m depth in the verge hears the reference leak from a main 3 m away
law: Hemispherical spreading of the leak's ground-borne power (efficiency 1e-5, soil density 1800 kg/m3, wave speed 200 m/s, Q 20) against 1e-08 m/s/rtHz urban ground noise (assumed): signal to noise +14 dB at 3 m, -6 dB with 10 x the ground noise, +4 dB at 10 x less efficiency, -6 dB at 10 m. Reach is a few metres, not the 100 m of option A
check: Ground noise and efficiency are unknown; a recording beside a known leak is TRL 4 work

claim: The 10 mm HDPE wall of the ground box carries the soil pressure at 0.5 m depth
law: One-way strip of the 0.30 m short side, sigma = 0.75 p L^2 / t^2 = 3.04 MPa at the at-rest pressure 4.5 kPa, against the 5 MPa long-term design stress used for HDPE in the sister repo TideFlap (an estimate); but the creep deflection of the strip at a long-term modulus of 250 MPa is 23 mm, about 8 % of the span, so the wall needs ribs or more thickness; traffic or foot surcharge on the verge and the lid (not rated for vehicles) are not checked
check: Stress passes, stiffness does not: ribs or a 15 mm wall to propose (LKL-RSK-001)

claim: A stainless spike driven 0.5 m into soil couples the geophone to the ground and survives driving
law: A 22 mm spike with a cone tip is a standard geophone spike geometry; driving through stony or compacted verge may bend it and a buried pipe can be struck (a strike hazard, risk register)
check: Soil and utility records to check at each site; no test at TRL 3
